cues.subtitle: Alice, Hub, Bob, Carol and Dave register as entities on the Depository contract. Hub will act as a dealer; the others are its customers.
cues.title: Five banks join the Depository
cues.tradfiParallel: Banks with accounts in the same settlement system, trading FX through a dealer bank.
cues.what: Alice, Hub, Bob, Carol and Dave register as entities on the Depository contract. Hub will act as a dealer; the others are its customers.
cues.why: This scenario shows foreign exchange inside bilateral accounts: two currencies, one dealer, and no pooled exchange account.

cues.subtitle: Alice opens one bilateral account with Hub. It can carry several currencies side by side.
cues.title: Alice opens an account with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: A bilateral dealing relationship with a single co-signed record per counterparty.
cues.what: Alice opens one bilateral account with Hub. It can carry several currencies side by side.
cues.why: Every trade Alice makes with Hub will be a change to this one account, signed by both.

cues.subtitle: Alice and Hub grant each other 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC of credit.
cues.title: Credit lines in two currencies
cues.tradfiParallel: Bilateral FX settlement limits, one per currency, unsecured.
cues.what: Alice and Hub grant each other 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC of credit.
cues.why: Each bank sets how much the other may owe it, per currency, with no collateral behind it here. Trades settle inside the accounts within these limits, without moving reserves first.

cues.subtitle: Hub enables a WETH/USDC order book. Customers send orders through their own account with Hub; Hub matches them.
cues.title: Hub opens an order book
cues.tradfiParallel: A dealer internalising client FX flow, with every client's settlement confined to its own account.
cues.what: Hub enables a WETH/USDC order book. Customers send orders through their own account with Hub; Hub matches them.
cues.why: Hub never takes custody of a pooled balance. Each fill is a change to the customer's own bilateral account, which the customer co-signs.

cues.subtitle: Bob opens an account with Hub and they exchange the same credit lines: 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC each way.
cues.title: Bob connects to Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: Two clients of the same dealer bank, each with its own settlement line.
cues.what: Bob opens an account with Hub and they exchange the same credit lines: 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC each way.
cues.why: Alice and Bob never need an account with each other. Hub intermediates, and each side's risk stays inside its own account with Hub.

cues.subtitle: On a local test chain, Hub runs a WETH/USDC order book. Alice and Bob each have one account with Hub, with credit lines of 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC each way and no collateral; nobody holds reserves on the Depository.
cues.title: Starting point: a dealer and two customers
cues.tradfiParallel: Two clients of a dealer bank, each with its own unsecured settlement limits.
cues.what: On a local test chain, Hub runs a WETH/USDC order book. Alice and Bob each have one account with Hub, with credit lines of 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC each way and no collateral; nobody holds reserves on the Depository.
cues.why: Every trade will be a change to a customer's own account with the dealer, signed by both. With credit lines alone, each side's exposure is unsecured up to its limits.

cues.subtitle: Alice places a limit order: sell 20 WETH for 60,000 USDC, 3,000 USDC per WETH. The order sits in her account with Hub.
cues.title: Alice offers 20 WETH
cues.tradfiParallel: A resting limit order with a dealer, pre-validated against the client's settlement line.
cues.what: Alice places a limit order: sell 20 WETH for 60,000 USDC, 3,000 USDC per WETH. The order sits in her account with Hub.
cues.why: The offer is part of the co-signed account state, so the capacity it uses is reserved and cannot be promised twice.

cues.subtitle: Bob bids for 10 WETH at up to 3,100 USDC per WETH. Hub matches him against Alice at her price. Each customer settles with Hub in their own account: Alice delivers 10 WETH and receives 30,000 USDC; Bob receives 10 WETH and pays at Alice's price, below his limit.
cues.title: Bob buys 10 WETH: Alice and Bob each settle with Hub
cues.tradfiParallel: Not CLS: bilateral claims on the dealer inside unsecured credit lines, with no multilateral netting and no central bank money. In common with payment-versus-payment: each customer's two legs move together.
cues.what: Bob bids for 10 WETH at up to 3,100 USDC per WETH. Hub matches him against Alice at her price. Each customer settles with Hub in their own account: Alice delivers 10 WETH and receives 30,000 USDC; Bob receives 10 WETH and pays at Alice's price, below his limit.
cues.why: Inside each account both currency legs change in one co-signed frame, so neither customer delivers one currency without receiving the other. The two accounts update separately; between them, Hub carries the risk.

keyMetrics: Filled: 10 WETH at 3,000 USDC per WETH
cues.subtitle: Hub matched Bob against Alice. In Alice's account she delivered 10 WETH and received 30,000 USDC; in Bob's account he received 10 WETH and paid for it in USDC at Alice's price. Each frame is co-signed by the customer and the dealer.
cues.title: Filled at Alice's price: 10 WETH
cues.tradfiParallel: Each client's two legs settled together in its own account with the dealer.
cues.what: Hub matched Bob against Alice. In Alice's account she delivered 10 WETH and received 30,000 USDC; in Bob's account he received 10 WETH and paid for it in USDC at Alice's price. Each frame is co-signed by the customer and the dealer.
cues.why: The fill is now part of each customer's own account state. Nothing reached the Depository: these are bilateral positions inside the credit lines.

cues.subtitle: Alice cancels the unfilled 10 WETH of her order. Hub co-signs the cancellation and the reserved capacity is released.
cues.title: Alice cancels the rest
cues.tradfiParallel: Withdrawing a resting order with a dealer.
cues.what: Alice cancels the unfilled 10 WETH of her order. Hub co-signs the cancellation and the reserved capacity is released.
cues.why: A cancellation is a signed account change like any other, so both sides agree exactly what is still open.

cues.subtitle: Alice offers 20 WETH for 60,000 USDC again. This time she will stop responding halfway through.
cues.title: A second order: 20 WETH
cues.tradfiParallel: Replacement-cost risk, not principal risk: Alice's signed order makes her leg enforceable, and Hub pays her nothing until it is.
cues.what: Alice offers 20 WETH for 60,000 USDC again. This time she will stop responding halfway through.
cues.why: The next steps show what protects the dealer when a customer disappears between two legs of a trade.

cues.subtitle: Bob buys 8 WETH, 40% of Alice's order. Hub matches it and settles Bob's side, but Alice has gone offline and never co-signs her side of the fill.
cues.title: Bob buys 40% while Alice goes offline
cues.tradfiParallel: One side of a dealer's back-to-back trade settled, the other counterparty silent: a replacement-cost exposure.
cues.what: Bob buys 8 WETH, 40% of Alice's order. Hub matches it and settles Bob's side, but Alice has gone offline and never co-signs her side of the fill.
cues.why: Hub has settled with Bob and is owed the matching leg by Alice. It has paid Alice nothing, so what it risks is the cost of replacing her leg, not the principal.

cues.subtitle: Hub takes the Alice account to the Depository. The claim carries the last co-signed state plus the matched fill ratio, 40%, as evidence.
cues.title: Hub disputes with the fill as evidence
cues.tradfiParallel: Close-out of an unsettled FX trade, enforced from the matched confirmation instead of trust.
cues.what: Hub takes the Alice account to the Depository. The claim carries the last co-signed state plus the matched fill ratio, 40%, as evidence.
cues.why: Alice signed the order; the fill ratio proves how much of it was matched. The Depository can enforce Alice's leg without her cooperation.

cues.subtitle: Hub submits the dispute to the Depository. Alice has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; the demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.title: Dispute filed: the challenge window opens
cues.tradfiParallel: Filing a claim with a set period for the counterparty to contest it.
cues.what: Hub submits the dispute to the Depository. Alice has 25 hours to answer with a newer co-signed state; the demo fast-forwards the clock.
cues.why: An older state loses only if the other side answers in time with a newer one, so each bank — or a watchtower — must watch the chain during the window. Alice has nothing newer: the fill is the latest thing she agreed to.

cues.subtitle: The challenge window ends with no newer state from Alice. The dispute finalization is drafted and submitted with the fill ratio attached.
cues.title: Window closes: finalization submitted
cues.tradfiParallel: The contest period lapses and the claim becomes enforceable.
cues.what: The challenge window ends with no newer state from Alice. The dispute finalization is drafted and submitted with the fill ratio attached.
cues.why: A deadline, not a negotiation, ends the dispute.

cues.subtitle: The Depository finalizes the account from the evidence, including Alice's 40% fill, and the account stays closed. These accounts run on credit lines alone, with no reserves or collateral on the Depository, so any amount one side still owes the other is booked on-chain as a debt in that currency.
cues.title: Dispute settled on-chain
cues.tradfiParallel: The Depository applies the latest co-signed state mechanically; legal finality depends on governing law.
cues.what: The Depository finalizes the account from the evidence, including Alice's 40% fill, and the account stays closed. These accounts run on credit lines alone, with no reserves or collateral on the Depository, so any amount one side still owes the other is booked on-chain as a debt in that currency.
cues.why: Hub's claim for the leg it settled with Bob is now an on-chain claim on Alice, created without her cooperation. What it recovers depends on her future reserves: credit without collateral is only as good as the debtor.

cues.subtitle: Carol and Dave open accounts with Hub and exchange the same two-currency credit lines: 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC each way.
cues.title: Carol and Dave connect
cues.tradfiParallel: New clients onboarded to a dealer with their own settlement lines.
cues.what: Carol and Dave open accounts with Hub and exchange the same two-currency credit lines: 100 WETH and 300,000 USDC each way.
cues.why: Adding a participant adds one bilateral account with the dealer. Nobody else's account changes.

cues.subtitle: Carol places a large sell order: 40 WETH at 2,900 USDC per WETH.
cues.title: Carol offers 40 WETH
cues.tradfiParallel: A large resting offer with a dealer, filled in parts.
cues.what: Carol places a large sell order: 40 WETH at 2,900 USDC per WETH.
cues.why: Large orders rest in the book until buyers arrive; each partial fill settles on its own.

cues.subtitle: Dave bids for 10 WETH at up to 3,000 USDC per WETH and is filled at Carol's 2,900 USDC per WETH. Carol receives 29,000 USDC.
cues.title: Dave buys 10 WETH at Carol's price
cues.tradfiParallel: Each client's two legs move together in its own account with the dealer.
cues.what: Dave bids for 10 WETH at up to 3,000 USDC per WETH and is filled at Carol's 2,900 USDC per WETH. Carol receives 29,000 USDC.
cues.why: The trade settles in the two bilateral accounts with Hub, Carol's and Dave's, each with both of its legs in one signed frame.

keyMetrics: Filled: 10 WETH at 2,900 USDC per WETH
cues.subtitle: Dave was filled at Carol's 2,900 USDC per WETH, below his limit. Carol's account and Dave's account with Hub each changed by one co-signed frame with both legs.
cues.title: Filled at Carol's price: 10 WETH
cues.tradfiParallel: Each client's two legs move together in its own account with the dealer.
cues.what: Dave was filled at Carol's 2,900 USDC per WETH, below his limit. Carol's account and Dave's account with Hub each changed by one co-signed frame with both legs.
cues.why: Price improvement goes to the buyer: he pays the resting seller's price.

keyMetrics: Asks: 30 WETH at 2,900 USDC, 20 WETH at 3,100 USDC
cues.subtitle: Carol adds a second offer: 20 WETH at 3,100 USDC per WETH. The book now has two price levels.
cues.title: Carol adds 20 WETH at 3,100 USDC per WETH
cues.tradfiParallel: A dealer's ladder of offers at increasing prices.
cues.what: Carol adds a second offer: 20 WETH at 3,100 USDC per WETH. The book now has two price levels.
cues.why: Each level is a separate signed offer inside Carol's account with Hub.

cues.subtitle: Dave buys 50 WETH with a limit of 3,200 USDC per WETH. Hub fills him across both levels: 30 WETH at 2,900 USDC and 20 WETH at 3,100 USDC.
cues.title: Dave sweeps the book
cues.tradfiParallel: An order walking a dealer's ladder, each fill settled with both legs together in the client's account.
cues.what: Dave buys 50 WETH with a limit of 3,200 USDC per WETH. Hub fills him across both levels: 30 WETH at 2,900 USDC and 20 WETH at 3,100 USDC.
cues.why: One order, several fills, every one settled with both legs in the bilateral accounts involved. The dealer ends flat; only the customers' positions changed.

cues.subtitle: Dave received 50 WETH across both price levels and paid 149,000 USDC; Carol received 149,000 USDC. Hub passed both legs through and ends flat on this trade.
cues.title: The book is swept
cues.tradfiParallel: An order walking a dealer's ladder, each fill settled with both legs together in the client's account.
cues.what: Dave received 50 WETH across both price levels and paid 149,000 USDC; Carol received 149,000 USDC. Hub passed both legs through and ends flat on this trade.
cues.why: Every fill settled inside the two customers' accounts with the dealer; no order is left resting.
